newsitem.title: ESTONIA: SHARE MARKET INVESTMENT RISES, FOREIGNERS ACTIVE.
newsitem.headline: SHARE MARKET INVESTMENT RISES, FOREIGNERS ACTIVE.

text.p: The Estonian Stock Exchange said on Thursday that investment in the market has leapt since November last year and foreign investors were increasing their total market share.
The bourse said in a statement that there was a 1.76 percent increase in total market share by foreign investors in companies listed on the Tallinn stock exchange between November and March.
Total investment in the market on March 13 was 11.6 billion kroons compared to November 1996's 5.6 billion kroons.
Estonian investment increased from 3.4 billion kroons in November to 6.9 billion kroons in March, the stock exchange said in a statement. The rest of the investments were by foreigners.
Investment from Estonia as a percentage of total investment decreased from 61.37 percent in November 1996 to 59.61 percent.

"The increase in foreign investment is important, but it is not too great and the increase in Estonian investment is good as it brings stability to the market," Helo Meigas, Tallinn Stock Exchange managing director, told Reuters.
In the same period Britain replaced Sweden as the third largest foreign investing country with 8.19 percent of total investment or 953.6 million kroons and Sweden on 940.7 million kroons.
